name: Paired scroll
description: Two open hourglass curves, held by a quiet outer frame. Small hanging ornaments and parallel center bars are removed.
principle: A straight perimeter makes the large curved voids legible. The opposing curls slow the eye at the top and bottom.

name: Lyre
description: A single elongated lyre with a linked pair of heart-shaped voids. The original mesh is removed and the scroll tips are opened.
principle: The narrow waist makes the top and foot feel generous. One continuous line carries the whole height.

name: Heart trellis
description: The complete four-lobed panel, with a lozenge crossing at its center. Secondary interior curls are reduced to four generous turns.
principle: The central diamond is made by the crossing curves themselves. Its tension offsets the soft heart-shaped ends.

name: Four-point rhythm
description: Two columns of large curved four-point forms. Rectangular grid rails and the photographic wire mesh are omitted.
principle: The star is a shaped void between four concave arcs. Repetition works because each interval is identical.

name: Oval chain
description: The Penang reference reduced to two elongated chains and four broad diamond anchors. Small intersections are enlarged.
principle: An oval reads as both a loop and the gap between two adjacent curves. Solid diamonds punctuate that soft rhythm.

name: Twin hearts
description: The whole paired-door rhythm becomes a single, balanced field. Large heart loops meet at one center; trim panels and knobs are omitted.
principle: Diagonal movement links the corners to the center. The same curve turns outward at the shoulders and inward at the waist.

name: Arched portal
description: A complete arched doorway contained on the 4:6 bar. The ornamental field has one large pair of curls above and below an open middle.
principle: A calm central interval prevents the arch and its curls from competing. The top silhouette does the architectural work.

name: Crowned gate
description: The scalloped crown and long diagonals define the entire gate. Rows of tiny rings, spearheads and tight curls are replaced by open sweeps.
principle: The crown concentrates activity at the top; long quiet uprights give it somewhere to rest.

name: Scroll vine
description: A full-height S-stem and two large side scrolls. Catalogue micro-leaves are replaced by a pair of broad leaf silhouettes.
principle: Large, medium and small turns are hierarchical. The stem changes curvature gradually instead of repeating identical tight spirals.

name: Heart palmette
description: A double-height central heart with broad palm-like shoulders. The vertical frame is complete and decorative joints become solid intersections.
principle: A heart is formed by two mirrored return curves. Letting the curves branch from the same stem makes the ornament feel grown rather than applied.
